# Reliability Checklist: A queued notification with no job is re-queued

**Purpose**: Requirements quality of the stranded queued-notification sweep: reliability, idempotence, no double send
**Created**: 2026-10-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: Reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact. `[x]` means the criterion is satisfied for requirements quality, not that implementation is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements stated for a send job that finishes between the sweep's read and its add (row no longer `queued`)? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases] — added edge case: the processor claims only `queued`/`held` rows, so the late add is a no-op
- [x] CHK002 Is the sweep's behaviour when one add fails part-way through a pass defined (rows after it)? [Completeness, Spec FR-008] — FR-008 ends the pass, the next sweep retries the rest
- [x] CHK003 Is the recovery requirement for a lost sweep schedule defined? [Completeness, Spec Edge Cases] — rescheduled on every worker start
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements stated for the sweep's own failed run (query error)? [Gap, Spec FR-008] — FR-008 now covers a failed read as well as a failed add

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Is "stale" defined with a number and a reference timestamp? [Clarity, Spec FR-002] — 5 minutes from `createdAt`
- [x] CHK006 Is "the add changes nothing" defined for every job state of an existing id? [Clarity, Spec FR-003] — waiting, delayed, active, kept failed
- [x] CHK007 Is "claim live or lapsed" unambiguous as to which field decides? [Clarity, Spec FR-004] — any non-null claim, per Key Entities

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK008 Do FR-004 and 522-FR-003 (lapsed claim lets the row's own job retry) agree on who may act on a lapsed claim? [Consistency, Spec FR-004] — FR-004 states the retry stays with the row's job, the sweep stays away
- [x] CHK009 Does the 5-minute window agree with the claim lapse time, so no live claim can look stale? [Conflict, Spec FR-002/FR-004] — not an issue: the sweep skips every claimed row, live or lapsed, whatever the window

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK010 Is "zero added jobs" in SC-002 tied to enumerated row states? [Measurability, Spec SC-002] — claim, mark, held, sent, existing job
- [x] CHK011 Can SC-001's 10 minutes be verified, given interval and window are assumptions? [Measurability, Spec SC-001] — stated as interval plus window, both named in Assumptions

## Edge Case and Recovery Coverage

- [x] CHK012 Are concurrent sweeps (two workers) covered? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases] — same job id, one add ignored
- [x] CHK013 Is a poison row (job kept failed) shown not to loop? [Coverage, Spec Clarifications] — no-op while kept, no removal
- [x] CHK014 Is the "provider took it, record failed" path shielded from the sweep? [Coverage, Spec FR-006] — claim kept
- [x] CHK015 Is the lost-sweep-on-an-all-down-queue backlog (many rows) bounded or explicitly unbounded? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions] — explicitly no cap
- ~~CHK016 Are PostgreSQL-down requirements defined?~~ — N/A: the row store is the truth and an outage stops the whole worker, not only the sweep (covered by CHK004)
